title: Stereotype
description: A typed marker that adds virtual attributes, default property values and, for tables, inherited columns, keys, indexes and checks.

key.description: The immutable kebab-case key that elements list in stereotypes.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

excludeStereotypes.description: Stereotype keys that a database schema's or a package's defaultStereotypes would give this element, left out with the stereotypes they imply. Only defaults can be excluded (MQ2029).

group.description: A label, not a link: an element carries at most one stereotype of a group, its own and implied ones together (MQ2013).

requires.description: Stereotype keys an element that carries this one must also carry (MQ2014).

conflicts.description: Stereotype keys an element that carries this one must not carry (MQ2015).

implies.description: Stereotype keys applied with this one, one level deep: an element that carries it carries them too, before its own stereotypes (MQ2017 refuses a stereotype that implies one that implies others).

parameters.description: Typed parameters, shaped like an extension file: a JSON Schema per property name (x-ref and x-translatable included) and the names each carrier must have. Values stay in the element's properties; defaults live in defaultProperties (MQ2018, MQ2019).

properties.description: A JSON Schema properties object: one schema per parameter name.

required.description: The parameters each carrier must have, judged on its merged values (the stereotype's defaults count).

defaultProperties.description: Default property values, merged under each carrier's own properties; each is checked against its own schema in parameters, without required (MQ2018).

storage.description: Table storage parameters the stereotype gives every table that carries it (a reusable tuning profile such as high-churn), per dialect; a table's own storage overrides a parameter, and a later stereotype overrides an earlier one.

columns.description: Columns every table that carries the stereotype inherits (its members, with the keys, indexes and checks below), keyed <table key>.<member id> in each table. A synthesized table that already stores the stereotype's attributes as columns inherits no member. A contributed column takes no attribute or sequence (MQ2024).

primaryKey.description: A primary key every carrier inherits, over the stereotype's own columns; no name, since every carrier would share it (MQ2024). A table with another primary key reports MQ4076.

uniques.description: Unique constraints every carrier inherits, over the stereotype's own columns (MQ2025), without a name (MQ2024).

foreignKeys.description: Foreign keys every carrier inherits, from the stereotype's own columns. The target is one fixed table (referencesTable) or the table each carrier names in a parameter (referencesParameter: a required string parameter typed x-ref kind table with sameDatabase), never both (MQ2026).

columns.description: Ids of the stereotype's columns, in key order.

referencesTable.description: The id of the one table every carrier references.

referencesParameter.description: The name of the stereotype parameter in which each carrier names the table it references (a table of its own database).

referencesColumns.description: With referencesTable: the referenced column ids; empty means the referenced primary key. Not with referencesParameter (MQ2026).

checks.description: Check constraints every carrier inherits, without a name (MQ2024). Their SQL names the stereotype's columns by their physical names, which a table cannot redefine.

indexes.description: Indexes every carrier inherits, over the stereotype's own columns (MQ2025), without a name (MQ2024).

errors.description: Errors every operation that carries the stereotype inherits, each keyed <operation id>.<error id> in the operation; an operation can redefine one's input, displayName and description, or exclude it. A stereotype with errors applies to operations (MQ3029).
